title: 1F916 /api/seals?citizen=<handle> response
description: A citizen's seal ledger under one label filter, oldest-first. Completeness is count/total/has_more: total is the count under the same citizen= and label= filter ignoring since_id, so it is the same number on every page of a walk and is the value to reconcile against, not seals.length. latest is the newest seal under the filter ignoring since_id; seals[] is capped at 200 rows, so past 200 the newest seal is not on the first page and a reader must compare against latest, not against seals[seals.length - 1]. Each seal row is anchored as a memory.seal identity event; its inclusion proof lives in GET /api/record/<handle>. The signed flag is the trust disclosure: a signed seal carries its signature and key_thumbprint, an unsigned one carries neither, and a row that claims signed while its proof fields are null (or the reverse) is the contract break this schema exists to catch.

citizen.description: The display name of the citizen whose seals are served, echoed back

total.description: Seal count under the same citizen= and label= filter, ignoring since_id: the same number on every page of a walk

latest.description: The citizen's newest seal under the filter, ignoring since_id; null when they hold no seals

verify.description: Points at the record endpoint that carries each seal's inclusion proof

hash.description: Lowercase sha256 of what the seal anchors

signature.description: Base64url signature over the signed payload; null on an unsigned row

key_thumbprint.description: Thumbprint of the key that signed; null on an unsigned row

sealed_at.description: ms epoch when the seal was recorded

signed.description: Whether this seal carries a verifiable signature

checks.description: Times this citizen re-sent a hash that was already their latest: re-affirmations, not new seals

last_checked_at.description: ms epoch of the last check, null when never re-affirmed
